findings.question: Does customizer-regressions run only when detect-changes reports code/e2e changes?
findings.answer: Yes, by per-STEP gating, not a job-level if. .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml at 6e21b530b, the new block starting at the line '  customizer-regressions:' declares 'needs: [detect-changes, install-deps]', 'runs-on: ubuntu-latest', 'timeout-minutes: 20' and NO job-level 'if:'. Every working step carries "if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.code == 'true' || needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e == 'true'", and the first step is "- name: Skip (no code or e2e changes)" with "if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.code != 'true' && needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e != 'true'". The detect-changes 'code' filter includes '.github/workflows/**' and '.github/actions/**', so a PR that edits this workflow triggers its own gate.

findings.question: Does the lint-and-test aggregator include it in needs and fail on its failure, while docs-only PRs still pass?
findings.answer: Yes on all three. The diff adds the line '        customizer-regressions,' to the lint-and-test needs list, bringing it to 19 members. The aggregator step runs jq over toJSON(needs) selecting '.value.result != "success"' and exits 1 on any hit, so a failed customizer-regressions turns the required 'Lint and Test' context red. Docs-only PRs: detect-changes and install-deps both always run and succeed (install-deps carries no 'if:'), so customizer-regressions itself RUNS, executes only the echo Skip step, and reports 'success' — the needs chain stays green. This is also consistent with the aggregator's own comment ('no needed job carries a job-level `if:`, so anything other than success means a real failure upstream'), which the new job honors because it gates per-step.

findings.question: Is the Playwright argv exactly the frozen contract string in scripts/qc/openspec-ci-contracts.mjs?
findings.answer: Yes, byte-exact. openspec-ci-contracts.mjs line 146 holds run: 'node scripts/playwright/run-playwright.mjs test e2e/customizer-equipment-catalog.spec.ts e2e/customizer-record-sheet-rendering.spec.ts e2e/customizer-edit-recovery.spec.ts --project=chromium --retries=0 --trace=retain-on-failure'. openspec-workflow-contracts.mjs line 127 matches with strict equality (steps.filter(step => step?.run === requiredRun.run)), and the live validator reports workflowJobContracts=1/1 with errors=0, which is only reachable on an exact string match. The --retries=0 / --trace=retain-on-failure pairing is also semantically necessary: playwright.config.ts line 105 sets retries: 2 on CI and line 142 sets trace: 'on-first-retry', which records nothing at zero retries.

findings.question: Is production server startup consistent with scripts/playwright/run-playwright.mjs and playwright.config.ts?
findings.answer: Yes. (a) PORT — playwright.config.ts line 3 defaults e2ePort to 3600, line 299 forces PORT: String(e2ePort) into webServer.env, and line 9 sets baseURL to http://localhost:3600; the Next standalone server reads PORT, so the workflow correctly omits it. (b) MEKSTATION_E2E_SERVER_COMMAND — playwright.config.ts line 288 reads process.env.MEKSTATION_E2E_SERVER_COMMAND ?? 'npm run dev'; run-playwright.mjs lines 67-78 spread ...process.env first and only override that key under --prod-evidence (not passed here), so the workflow value survives intact. (c) HOSTNAME — node_modules/playwright/lib/plugins/webServerPlugin.js lines 88-92 merge { ...DEFAULT_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES, ...process.env, ...this._options.env }, so webServer.env is NOT a whitelist in the installed runtime and HOSTNAME='127.0.0.1' reaches the standalone server. (d) NEXT_PUBLIC_* — the workflow sets NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE and NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_TEST on the BUILD step, which is correct: NEXT_PUBLIC_ values are inlined at build time and the config's runtime NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE (line 300) cannot reach a prebuilt standalone bundle. (e) standalone hydration — package.json build is 'npm run sync:mm-data-config && node scripts/next/run-next.mjs build --webpack && node scripts/hydrate-next-standalone-multiplayer-server.mjs', and that hydrate script copies public/ into .next/standalone/public (lines 132-136) and .next/static into .next/standalone/.next/static (lines 160-168) with assertExists guards (lines 188-193), so record-sheet assets fetched before the build are actually served.

findings.question: Is the asset fetch step consistent with .github/actions/setup-node-and-install inputs?
findings.answer: Yes. The composite action declares exactly three inputs — node-version, skip-nextjs-cache, fetch-assets (action.yml lines 4-16). The job passes node-version: '22' and fetch-assets: 'true'; no unknown input name is used. Step ordering is correct and contract-enforced: setup (fetch-assets) then npm run validate:assets:strict then npm run build then the browser run, checked positionally by openspec-workflow-contracts.mjs lines 182-196.

findings.question: Any new action, dependency, secret, or permission beyond the approved YAML declaration?
findings.answer: No. The only 'uses:' lines the diff adds are actions/checkout@v6, ./.github/actions/setup-node-and-install, actions/cache@v5 and actions/upload-artifact@v7 — all already present in pr-checks.yml at the base 13e4b9ea1 (22, 20, 2 and 4 occurrences respectively).
